clue.text: Drink picked up for Scandinavian

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by the ear, as on a radio, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does, with the tongue

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink to bring over for a Swedish or Norwegian friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lapp is a member of the Sami people of northern Scandinavia, an older name now often thought offensive.

clue.text: Substitute's back pass? Let me think

indicators.note: going back means reading the mountain pass word from its end to its start

blocks.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
the hesitating noise someone makes while thinking

explanation.surface: A footballer standing in for a regular wonders whether to pass the ball backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back pass' reads like a football term, but 'back' reverses the pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric temporarily standing in for another, so a substitute.

clue.text: Media silence about northern recruiters?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the silencing word wraps the northern letter

blocks.note: the press is the news media
to gag someone is to silence them
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A news blackout around recruiters operating in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The press gang forcibly enlisted men into the Royal Navy in the 18th and 19th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang was a body of men who forced others into naval service, hence recruiters by force.

clue.text: See 19
Skilled people Sinatra played with succeeded

indicators.note: played suggests letters performed in a different arrangement, like notes reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Talented musicians did well backing Frank Sinatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Artisans are craftsmen, workers skilled in a particular trade or handicraft.

clue.text: Where Noah found himself high and dry?

definitions.text: Where Noah found himself high and dry?

blocks.clueFragment: Where Noah found himself high and dry?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone left stranded and helpless, as the idiom high and dry means
setter's reading: literally up a mountain and out of the water as the Flood receded

explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis the ark comes to rest on the mountains of this name as the waters go down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ararat is the mountain range where the Bible says Noah's ark grounded after the Flood, a high dry place.

clue.text: Beyond silly covering banker's last debt

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the silly word goes around the banker's final letter
last means only the final letter of the word before it is kept

blocks.note: over means beyond, as in over the hill
daft means silly
the last letter of banker

explanation.surface: A foolish loan has left someone owing the bank more than they can pay.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is money owed to a bank after withdrawing more than the account holds, a form of debt.

clue.text: Leader in Aerosmith quits festival compound

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the band's name is kept
quits means leaves, so that letter departs from the festival word

blocks.note: Easter is a Christian festival
the first letter of the band's name

explanation.surface: The frontman of a rock band walks out of a music festival.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Order Yuan when travelling all the time?

indicators.note: things travelling are moved about, so these letters shift into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to get Chinese currency every time you go abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; the yuan is China's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Something year-round happens in every season, so continually, all the time.

clue.text: Very impressive record in charge

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone is running a remarkable recording session.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is informal for grand or spectacular, from the scale of heroic poems.

clue.text: Moved to palace that houses King and Queen

indicators.note: a building that houses something holds it inside, so the royal letter goes in
moved means shifted about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A royal couple relocated to a grand residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King and Queen' reads as one royal pair, but King gives a letter and Queen is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling queen of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: More old paintings recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the paintings word is read backwards

blocks.note: ex means former
paintings are art

explanation.surface: Someone remembers yet more old paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, so more as an adjective, as in extra time or more time.

clue.text: See 28
Whose words may lead to action?

definitions.text: Whose words may lead to action?

blocks.clueFragment: Whose words may lead to action?
blocks.note: surface reading: an inspiring speaker who stirs people to act
setter's reading: action in the legal sense, a lawsuit for defamation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' here is a court case, as in bringing an action for damages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who utters false damaging statements about another may be sued for defamation.

clue.text: Leaves when group performing inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the playing band goes into the word for when

blocks.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
a musical group
a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: Someone walks out while a band is playing within.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandons and leaves are both verbs meaning deserts or goes away from.

clue.text: Criminal ran brothel — not entirely detestable?

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the last letter of the word is cut
criminal means crooked or wrong, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain operated a house of ill repute, which is hardly admirable.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent things inspire loathing, so they are detestable; both are adjectives.

clue.text: Couple protest about 101 bound by the dozen?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the protest word wraps around the Roman number

blocks.note: a duo is a pair
a demo is a demonstration, a protest march
C is 100 and I is 1 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A pair demonstrate around something, tied up by the twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: Duodecimo (12mo) is a book size in which each printed sheet is folded into twelve leaves, so it is 'bound by the dozen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Duodecimo is a book format made of sheets folded into twelve leaves before binding.

clue.text: Secure gold in horse-drawn carriage

blocks.note: to land a deal is to secure it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Bullion is loaded safely into a coach and four.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled carriage pulled by horses, with a folding top.

clue.text: The German Renaissance painter — one to advise more greens?

blocks.note: die is a German word for the
Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A German Renaissance artist who championed vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The German' is not a nationality but the German article, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietitian is an expert in nutrition who might recommend eating more vegetables.

clue.text: Seducer, reluctant, brought to a Brazilian port

blocks.note: loth is a variant spelling of loath, unwilling
taken as written
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A womaniser, though unwilling, is taken to a harbour in Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a man who seduces women, from a character in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: Line in 28 12 disrupted again? How to hear yodelling? All shh!

annotation.answer: HIGH ON A HILL WAS A LONELY GOATHERD

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the following letters are scrambled

blocks.clueFragment: again? How to hear yodelling? All shh
blocks.note: the words taken as written, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A grumbling theatregoer wants silence so the yodelling can be heard properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the cross-referenced film; the line opens The Lonely Goatherd, the yodelling song from The Sound of Music.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the opening words of The Lonely Goatherd, a song from the musical film.

clue.text: See 19
Mammoth upset over book about forest dweller

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down entry flips the word upside down

blocks.note: mammoth means huge
B is the abbreviation for book
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A woolly mammoth knocks over a book about woodland animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mammoth' looks like the beast, but it is the adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibbons are small apes living in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Wrong to stop assistant turning to reload

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so the wrong word is pushed into the helper word
turning means facing about, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a helper is an assistant
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: An aide makes a mistake while restocking.
explanation.walkthrough: The wrong goes in just after the first letter of the helper, then the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to refill or restock, so to load again.

clue.text: Box in church for coins

blocks.note: to pen is to box in or enclose
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A collection box in church for donations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box in' reads as one verb, but 'in' just places the pen beside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence are British coins, the plural of penny.

clue.text: See 19
Too small to be consumed by a large duck

indicators.note: something consumed ends up inside the eater, so the small letter goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
S is the abbreviation for small
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A tiny morsel is eaten by a big duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are both adverbs meaning in addition, as well.

clue.text: Cold fish served up with hot worm

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means sent upwards, so these letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
an eel is a fish
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A chilled fish dish is presented with a warm worm.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking annelid, a segmented worm.

clue.text: Drunken nuisance embodies listlessness

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within one's body, so the answer sits inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A sozzled pest embodies apathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French-derived word for weary boredom, a lack of energy or interest.

clue.text: County in Belgium — risk here, unusually

indicators.note: unusually means in an unexpected way, so the letters are put in an unexpected order

blocks.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that some Belgian district is unusually dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County in Belgium' reads as one phrase, but the county is English and 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Berkshire is a county in southern England, west of London.

clue.text: Film spoils much fun, so it does

indicators.note: spoiling something ruins its form, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: the words taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumpy critic says a movie ruins all the enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sound of Music is the 1965 musical film starring Julie Andrews as Maria.

clue.text: Winger losing front part of foot

indicators.note: losing its front means the bird word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a winger is a bird, and a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A wide footballer misses the front of his foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests football, but it is something with wings; 'foot' is the twelve-inch measure, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a twelfth of a foot in imperial measurement.
